MA-Q-0222.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy completed its routine annual self-inspection three months ago. It now relocates to a new address, and a Board inspector arrives without prior notice shortly afterward. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The relocation triggers another Board-tool self-inspection within the regulatory timeframe even though the annual self-inspection was recent.
The Board may inspect the licensed pharmacy without prior notice.
The pharmacy may decline to provide requested pharmacy records because the inspection was unannounced.
The recent annual self-inspection prevents another self-inspection from being required during the same calendar year.
The pharmacy should provide documents requested by the Board or its designee in connection with the inspection.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.19 separately requires self-inspection after specified operational changes, including relocation, while 247 CMR 9.24 authorizes unannounced Board inspection and requires the pharmacy to provide requested documents. The recent annual self-inspection does not cancel the relocation-triggered duty or the Board's inspection authority.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: relocation creates a separate self-inspection trigger.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the Board may inspect without prior notice.
choice_analysis.C: The regulation requires requested documents to be provided.
choice_analysis.D: Annual completion does not eliminate the relocation-triggered inspection duty.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: requested documents must be supplied in connection with the inspection.

explanation.mpje_trap: A recent self-inspection is not a shield against either a triggered self-inspection or an unannounced Board inspection.

MA-RW-0075.stem:
An identified Board investigator visits a Massachusetts resident pharmacy without advance notice and requests completed self-inspection records relevant to an inspection. The Manager of Record is on vacation. The pharmacist on duty can access the requested records but is told by an employee that only the Manager of Record may release them. The pharmacy completed its annual self-inspection last week.

What should the pharmacist on duty do? Select ONE answer.

Provide a statement that the annual self-inspection was completed in place of the requested records.

Give the investigator access to the requested records as part of the pharmacy's inspection response.

MA-Q-0195.stem: A non-OTP practitioner plans to manage a patient's OUD by directly dispensing three-day supplies of methadone every week for the next month. The practitioner has not arranged a treatment referral and says each episode should be lawful because no individual supply will exceed three days. Which assessment is most accurate?

choices.text: The plan is permitted because each separate dispensing episode is limited to no more than a three-day supply
The plan is permitted if the practitioner documents a new emergency before each weekly dispensing episode
The plan does not fit the exception: it is a short emergency bridge while referral is being arranged, and the emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended
The plan is prohibited only because methadone may never be dispensed by a non-OTP practitioner under any emergency circumstance
The plan becomes permissible if a community pharmacy records each weekly dispensing episode in the patient's profile

explanation.core_reasoning: The federal non-OTP emergency provision is not a recurring maintenance mechanism. It permits a practitioner to dispense a limited emergency supply while arrangements for referral are being made, and the emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Staying at or below three days per episode does not authorize serial weekly use of the emergency exception.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Re-labeling each planned episode as a new emergency does not avoid the no-renewal/no-extension and referral requirements.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The pathway is a temporary bridge tied to arranging referral, not a substitute for ongoing maintenance treatment.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Federal law does contain a narrow non-OTP emergency dispensing provision.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. Pharmacy documentation cannot transform a recurring maintenance plan into a lawful use of the practitioner's emergency exception.

related_facts: Under the current rule, the practitioner may dispense up to a three-day supply at one time while arranging referral.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating the three-day quantity ceiling as a renewable weekly maintenance authority instead of reading the referral and no-extension limits together.

MA-RW-0076.stem:
The Board directed a pharmacy to submit an initial plan of correction within ten days. The pharmacy submitted it on time, but the Board returned it as unacceptable because a promise to retrain staff did not identify corrective actions for each violation, responsible individuals, or implementation dates. Which steps are consistent with the plan-of-correction requirements? Select ALL that apply.

Use a new twenty-one-day submission period because the first plan was returned rather than approved.
Have both the Manager of Record and the pharmacist licensee supervising the MOR's practice sign the plan.
Submit the revised plan within seven days after the unacceptable plan is returned to the pharmacy.
Postpone corrective work until the Board approves the revised plan and schedules a follow-up inspection.

explanation.core_reasoning: 초기 계획의 Board 지정 10일과 반려 후 revised plan의 7일을 구분한다. 계획에는 위반별 조치·예상일·책임자를 담고 MOR 및 해당 supervising licensee가 서명한다. 제출 일정만 맞추고 실제 compliance 달성을 뒤로 미루지는 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: §9.25(2)는 각 위반에 대응하는 corrective action, 예상 완료 또는 시행일, 각 조치의 책임자를 요구한다. 기존의 일반적인 재교육 약속에 이 요소들을 구체적으로 추가해야 한다.
choice_analysis.B: §9.25(1)의 기본 21일 또는 Board가 지정한 initial-plan 기간과 §9.25(5)의 returned unacceptable plan 이후 revised-plan 기간은 별도다. 반환되었다고 초기 21일이 재시작하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.E: §9.25(4)는 법규 준수를 가능한 한 신속하게 달성하도록 한다. 수정계획의 제출·승인 과정과 실제 시정조치는 구별하며, 모든 조치를 후속 inspection까지 미루라는 허가가 아니다.

MA-Q-0262.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist resolved a criminal matter in another state by admitting to sufficient facts, and the case was continued without a finding and later dismissed. She tells the Board she has no conviction to report. How should that resolution be characterised for Board purposes?

choices.text: Not a conviction, because the case was ultimately dismissed by the court.
Not a conviction, because no sentence was ever imposed upon her.
Not a conviction, because the matter arose outside of the Commonwealth.
A conviction only if the Board separately finds that she committed the crime.
A conviction, because an admission to sufficient facts and a continuance without a finding are included.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.02 defines conviction to include any admission to or finding of sufficient facts to warrant a finding of guilt, regardless of adjudication, a continuance without a finding, and any plea of guilty or nolo contendere, of or to a crime in any jurisdiction, accepted by the court, whether or not a sentence has been imposed. Each of the features she relies on is expressly inside the definition.

choice_analysis.A: Regardless of adjudication is part of the definition, so a later dismissal does not remove it.
choice_analysis.B: The definition applies whether or not a sentence has been imposed.
choice_analysis.C: The definition reaches a crime in any jurisdiction.
choice_analysis.D: No separate Board finding is needed; the definition applies on its own terms.

MA-RW-0077.stem:
During a shift at a Massachusetts pharmacy, pharmacist L develops medication-related somnolence that prevents reliable prescription verification. The owner directs L to continue as the sole pharmacist because no dispensing error has reached a patient. Pharmacist M, who is being considered as a replacement, receives treatment for a medical condition but retains the ability to practice safely. No Board disciplinary decision has been made.

Which conclusions about these facts are supported by the impairment and public-risk grounds for discipline? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The owner’s authorization removes the impairment ground while L remains on the scheduled shift.
L’s continued practice may support discipline even though no dispensing error has reached a patient.
M’s ongoing medical treatment establishes the same impairment ground without further fitness-to-practice facts.
Once L’s impairment is established, the Board must revoke the license instead of considering another disciplinary action.
L’s documented inability to verify and M’s preserved ability to practice require different impairment assessments.

explanation.core_reasoning: 치료 여부 → 실제 업무 능력 → impaired 상태의 practice 또는 위험 발생 가능성 순서로 판단한다. 고용주 승인과 무사고 이력은 impaired practice 사유를 없애지 않으며, 반대로 치료를 받는다는 이유만으로 impairment를 확정하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(g)는 illness·drug·mental/physical condition 등으로 practice 능력이 impaired된 상태에서 실제 업무를 하는 것을 징계 사유로 정한다. 고용주의 근무 승인이나 인력 부족을 이 사유의 면제로 두지 않는다. Board가 어떤 최종 처분을 할지는 별도의 절차다.
choice_analysis.B: 지문은 L의 verification 능력이 실제로 손상됐다고 명시한다. 10.03(1)(g)의 impaired practice와 (k)의 public health·safety·welfare에 위험을 줄 capacity 또는 potential은 이미 환자에게 오류가 도달했어야만 적용되는 사유가 아니다. 사유가 성립할 수 있다는 판단을 자동 면허취소와 동일시하지 않는다.

MA-Q-0268.stem: Another jurisdiction sanctioned a Massachusetts pharmacist solely for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. The Board is considering discipline on the out-of-state ground. What is the correct outcome?

choices.text: Discipline may proceed, because out-of-state sanctions are a listed disciplinary ground.
Discipline may proceed if the Board first convenes an investigative conference.
Discipline may proceed but must be limited to an advisory letter in the file.
Discipline is deferred until the other jurisdiction resolves any pending appeal.
Discipline may not be imposed, because the protected activity carve-out overrides the listed grounds.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.03(3) applies notwithstanding the grounds for discipline in 247 CMR 10.03, so it overrides the out-of-state ground rather than sitting beside it. No licensee shall be subject to discipline for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services, or for any sanction arising from such services, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. Both qualifiers are met.

choice_analysis.A: The carve-out is expressed as operating notwithstanding those grounds.
choice_analysis.B: Procedure does not unlock a ground the carve-out removes.
choice_analysis.C: An advisory letter would still treat the protected activity as a basis for Board action.
choice_analysis.D: Deferral would keep the protected conduct alive as a basis.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the carve-out overrides, and both qualifiers are satisfied.

related_facts: Parallel protections appear at 247 CMR 3.05 for licensure and 247 CMR 8.08 for support personnel.
explanation.mpje_trap: The carve-out is written to override the grounds list, so pointing at a listed ground does not defeat it.

MA-Q-0223.stem: During an investigation, the Board finds conditions at a pharmacy that present an immediate and serious threat to public health and safety. Waiting for a final adjudicatory decision would leave the unsafe operation in place. Which Board response is most consistent with the Massachusetts disciplinary framework?

choices.text: The Board must wait for a final disciplinary hearing before restricting the pharmacy's operation or affected products.
The Board may use an appropriate summary cease-and-desist or quarantine mechanism, subject to the regulation's subsequent review procedures.
The Board can act only against the individual pharmacist and has no emergency authority directed at the pharmacy or affected products.
The Board must convert the matter into an advisory letter because emergency action cannot be disciplinary.
The Board may permanently revoke the pharmacy license without any procedural review because the threat is serious.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.00 provides summary mechanisms when an immediate and serious threat requires action before ordinary final adjudication, including cease-and-desist or quarantine tools in the circumstances defined by the regulation. Emergency authority does not mean the procedural review protections disappear.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation provides summary tools precisely because waiting may be unsafe.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: summary cease-and-desist or quarantine can address an immediate threat with review procedures afterward.
choice_analysis.C: The Board's framework can address pharmacy operations and products, not only an individual registrant.
choice_analysis.D: An advisory letter is not the emergency control mechanism described here.
choice_analysis.E: Seriousness does not eliminate all subsequent procedural review.

explanation.mpje_trap: Emergency authority permits action before final adjudication; it does not erase process.

MA-Q-0211.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives an advisory letter from the Board after a complaint review. A credentialing form later asks whether that Board outcome was formal disciplinary action. Based on the classification of the Board action itself, which response is most accurate?

choices.text: Yes. Any written Board communication resolving a complaint is formal discipline.
No. An advisory letter may be retained in Board files but is not itself formal disciplinary action.
Yes. An advisory letter is the same disciplinary category as probation.
No. The letter has no regulatory significance and may be treated as though it never existed.
Yes. The letter automatically suspends the pharmacist's registration until the next renewal.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.06 distinguishes an advisory letter from formal disciplinary sanctions. The pharmacist should characterize the Board outcome accurately: an advisory letter can remain in Board records, but the letter itself is not formal disciplinary action.

choice_analysis.A: Formal discipline is a defined category; an advisory letter is not automatically converted into discipline by being written.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the regulation distinguishes advisory letters from formal disciplinary action.
choice_analysis.C: Probation is a formal disciplinary sanction; an advisory letter is not the same category.
choice_analysis.D: The letter can remain in Board records even though it is not formal discipline.
choice_analysis.E: An advisory letter does not itself impose automatic suspension.

explanation.mpje_trap: Do not equate every Board communication with formal discipline.

MA-RW-0078.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist previously received an advisory letter. A later complaint is resolved by an agreement signed by the Board and the pharmacist. For twelve months, the agreement permits pharmacy practice subject to weekly supervision and specified monitoring conditions. The Board expressly designates this twelve-month arrangement as disciplinary. No formal adjudicatory hearing was held. A reviewer asks how this current arrangement is classified under 247 CMR 10.06.

Which classification fits the current arrangement? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An advisory action, because the complaint was resolved by agreement without an adjudicatory hearing.
A suspension of practice, because weekly supervision restricts the pharmacist’s independent work.
A reprimand, because the pharmacist may continue practicing and the Board retains the agreement in its file.
Disciplinary probation, with practice allowed subject to the conditions imposed by the Board.

explanation.core_reasoning: 조치의 실제 내용과 법정 정의를 확인한다. 합의에 따른 해결이라는 절차만으로 nondisciplinary라 판단하지 않고, probation의 조건부 practice와 suspension·revocation의 효과를 구분한다.

choice_analysis.A: 10.06(2)의 advisory letter는 formal discipline이 아니지만, 이전 letter의 분류를 후속 probation에 옮길 수 없다. 10.06(4)는 consent agreement에 따라 부과된 probation도 disciplinary action으로 명시한다. Hearing이 없었다는 점은 이를 advisory로 바꾸지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: Practice에 supervision 조건이 붙었다는 사실만으로 suspension으로 분류하지 않는다. 10.06(4)는 Board 조건 아래 practice할 수 있는 probation을 별도로 정하며, 이 agreement는 그 조건부 practice를 명시적으로 허용한다. 실제 practice 권한을 정지한 조치는 10.06(5)의 다른 분류다.
choice_analysis.C: Reprimand도 formal disciplinary action이지만, 계속 practice할 수 있다거나 Board file에 기록된다는 공통점만으로 조치의 종류를 정할 수 없다. 지문처럼 12개월 동안 Board가 supervision·monitoring 조건 아래 practice를 허용한 내용은 10.06(4)의 probation 정의에 해당한다. 10.06(3)의 reprimand와 조건부 practice 기간을 구별한다.
choice_analysis.D: 10.06(4)는 probation을 disciplinary action으로 정하고 formal hearing 또는 consent agreement로 부과한 조건 아래 practice할 수 있는 기간이라고 설명한다. 지문의 12개월 supervision·monitoring 조건을 그 정의에 적용한다. 과거 advisory letter와 현재 agreement는 각각의 실제 내용으로 분류하며, 별도 credentialing form의 공개 질문에는 그 양식의 문구도 읽어야 한다.

MA-Q-0123.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives an otherwise valid written methylphenidate prescription. The prescriber indicates that a state electronic-prescribing exception or waiver applies, but the pharmacist has no practical way to verify whether the prescriber properly qualifies for that exception. The pharmacist must independently prove the prescriber’s exception before considering any other prescription-validity requirement.
The pharmacist must reject every nonelectronic controlled-substance prescription even when an exception or waiver may apply.
The pharmacist must contact the Board for case-by-case permission before dispensing any written prescription.
The pharmacist may ignore all other controlled-substance requirements once the prescriber mentions an electronic-prescribing exception.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts places the electronic-prescribing compliance obligation on the prescriber without making the dispensing pharmacist the verifier of the prescriber’s exception or waiver. Section 721.070(C) says the pharmacist receiving an otherwise valid written or oral prescription is not required to verify that exception status. Other prescription requirements still apply.

choice_analysis.A: This states the pharmacist-facing no-verification rule in 105 CMR 721.070(C).
choice_analysis.B: The regulation expressly avoids imposing that exception-verification duty on the pharmacist receiving an otherwise valid prescription.
choice_analysis.C: Exceptions and waivers are part of the framework, so nonelectronic form alone is not an automatic pharmacist-side rejection rule.
choice_analysis.D: The regulation does not require routine Board preclearance for each otherwise valid written prescription.
choice_analysis.E: No-verification of the e-prescribing exception does not waive schedule, legitimacy, content, or other dispensing requirements.

explanation.mpje_trap: ‘Not required to verify the exception’ is not the same as ‘not required to verify anything about the prescription.’

explanation.core_reasoning: 기존 grant의 날짜로 5주년을 계산하고, 후속 petition의 접수와 실제 grant를 구분한다. 새 petition은 기존 승인을 단순 연장하는 서류가 아니라 요건을 다시 충족해야 하는 신청이며, impractical과 unduly burdensome도 AND다.

choice_analysis.A: 14.01(5)(b)는 2013-06-30 이후 부여한 waiver가 grant의 5주년에 만료된다고 정한다. (c)는 만료 전후에 subsequent petition을 제출할 수 있게 하지만 pending filing에 자동 연장 효과를 주지 않는다. (d)는 subsequent waiver가 실제로 granted됐는지를 기준으로 한다.

choice_analysis.D: 14.01(1)(b)와 (3)(c)는 impractical AND unduly burdensome을 함께 쓴다. 둘 중 하나만 제시해도 충분하다는 OR로 단순화하지 않는다. 또한 public interest와 safeguards도 별개의 필수 판단 요소다. 요건 제시와 Board의 실제 grant는 여전히 다른 단계다.

MA-Q-0095.stem: An adult asks a trained Massachusetts pharmacist to prescribe a self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive. She has never previously received a contraceptive prescription. What is the most accurate response under the pharmacist-prescribing statute?

Lack of a prior prescription is not itself a bar; the pharmacist still must follow the required screening and protocol process.
The pharmacist may prescribe any contraceptive dosage form because the patient has no prior prescription.
The patient must first obtain a controlled-substance registration because hormonal contraception is Schedule II.
The pharmacist may skip the self-screening risk assessment when the patient is a first-time user.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts expressly permits pharmacist prescribing of covered hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral products regardless of evidence of a previous prescription. choice_analysis.C: The authority remains limited to the product categories authorized by statute and protocol.
choice_analysis.D: The pathway is not created by treating hormonal contraception as Schedule II controlled-substance prescribing.
choice_analysis.E: The self-screening risk assessment is a required safeguard, including for a first-time requester.

MA-Q-0081.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is evaluating the current statutory qualifications to enter a collaborative practice agreement. Which statements reflect M.G.L. c.112, § 24B1/2(b)? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Hold a current Massachusetts pharmacist license, currently practice in the Commonwealth, and maintain at least $1,000,000 of professional liability insurance.
Have earned a PharmD degree or completed five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist, or the equivalent.
Devote a portion of practice to the defined drug-therapy area and complete at least five additional related CE contact hours in each agreement year.
Apply for the statute's limited MassHealth ordering/referring participation if implementing regulations governing that participation are promulgated.
A pharmacist with a current PharmD must also complete five years of licensed-practice experience because the degree alternative is no longer recognized by statute.

explanation.core_reasoning: The current statute lists licensure/current practice, $1 million liability coverage, a PharmD-or-five-years-or-equivalent qualification, therapy-area practice focus, five additional annual CE contact hours, and a conditional limited MassHealth participation application requirement. The statute does not state that every PharmD holder must also accumulate five years solely to satisfy subsection (b)(3).

choice_analysis.A: Correct. These are express statutory baseline qualifications.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. The current statutory text uses an alternative: PharmD, five years of licensed experience, or equivalent.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Practice focus and five additional related CE contact hours per agreement year are statutory requirements.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. The MassHealth limited-participation application duty is conditional on the implementing regulations described by the statute.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. It contradicts the current statutory PharmD-or-experience alternative.

related_facts: Promulgated regulations can add operational requirements, but an exam item should not use older regulatory wording to erase an alternative expressly present in the current statute.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not memorize an older grandfather formulation without checking the current statute.

MA-Q-0305.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is mapping out what a proposed collaborative practice agreement could cover. Which activities may fall within collaborative drug therapy management as the statute defines it? Select all that apply.

Collecting and reviewing the patient's history.
Obtaining and checking pulse, temperature, blood pressure and respiration.
Settling a diagnosis where a laboratory result plainly supports one.
Ordering and evaluating laboratory tests directly related to the drug therapy.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(a) defines collaborative drug therapy management as the initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing of a patient's drug therapy under an agreement, and provides that it may include collecting and reviewing histories, obtaining and checking the named vital signs, and ordering and evaluating laboratory tests directly related to drug therapy on the stated conditions.

choice_analysis.B: Correct: expressly included.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the four named vital signs are expressly included.
choice_analysis.D: The evaluation shall not include a diagnostic component.
choice_analysis.E: Correct, subject to physician supervision or direct consultation and an approved protocol.

related_facts: Laboratory work requires an approved protocol applicable to the practice setting
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume that a pharmacist who may order and evaluate a test may also act on what it shows.

MA-Q-0243.stem: A PharmD graduate of an ACPE-accredited school has accepted a pharmacy residency at a Massachusetts hospital and will begin next month. She has not yet passed NAPLEX or MPJE. Which arrangement satisfies the regulation?

choices.text: She may practise on the strength of her residency appointment and PharmD degree.
She may practise unsupervised because a residency is a Board-approved training program.
She may practise only after obtaining a Massachusetts pharmacist licence.
She must hold a Massachusetts pharmacy intern licence and be supervised by a pharmacist.
She must hold an out-of-state licence recognised for reciprocity.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.01(8) requires a PharmD graduate who has accepted a Massachusetts residency to apply for and obtain a pharmacy intern licence until obtaining a Massachusetts pharmacist licence, and provides that a graduate enrolled in a Massachusetts residency shall either hold a Massachusetts pharmacist licence or hold a Massachusetts intern licence and be supervised by a pharmacist.

choice_analysis.A: A residency appointment and a degree are not practice credentials.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation does not treat a residency as authorising unsupervised practice.
choice_analysis.C: A pharmacist licence is one permitted route, but the intern licence route is also available and is the applicable one here.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: an intern licence with pharmacist supervision is the applicable arrangement.
choice_analysis.E: Reciprocity is not the mechanism contemplated for this graduate.

related_facts: A pharmacy intern must work under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.
explanation.mpje_trap: A residency is a training position, not a licence; the graduate still needs one of two named credentials.

MA-RW-0027.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist first seeks a CDTM agreement in 2026 after three years of licensed practice. The pharmacist holds current Board of Pharmacy Specialties certification, has completed the practice site's comprehensive credentialing and training, and has current BLS certification. All other CDTM qualifications are satisfied.

How should the pharmacist assess the five-year experience requirement? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Wait for five years of licensed practice because certification cannot satisfy equivalency.
Complete an ASHP PGY2 residency in addition to the current BPS certification.
Use site credentialing alone as the recognized substitute for five years of practice.
Use the current BPS certification and completed site requirements as a recognized equivalency.

explanation.core_reasoning: 5년 실무와 Board가 인정한 동등성은 대안이다. 인정되는 경로를 실제로 충족했는지와 현장 추가 요건을 함께 확인한다. 과거 학위 grandfather 날짜의 경계는 이 문항의 정답 근거로 사용하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: Board advisory는 현재 유효한 BPS 인증을 인정되는 교육 동등성 경로 중 하나로 열거한다. 이 사례에서 5년 실무만을 유일한 경로로 보아 기다릴 필요는 없다.
choice_analysis.B: 현재 BPS 인증과 PGY2 경로는 모두 누적해야 하는 요건이 아니라 대안적인 경로이다. 별도의 현장 credentialing 요건은 사례에서 이미 충족했다.
choice_analysis.C: 현장 credentialing은 Board advisory II.B의 추가 요건이다. 이것만으로 II.A의 인정된 교육·경험 동등성 경로를 대체하지 않는다. 이 사례에서는 현재 BPS 인증이 II.A의 해당 경로를 충족한다.
choice_analysis.D: 현재 BPS 인증은 Board가 제시한 동등성 경로이다. 현장별 종합 credentialing·교육과 current BLS도 별도로 충족되어 있으므로 5년 미만이라는 사실만으로 배제하지 않는다.
